text:
alex: Hey all, first day! Unboxed my MacBook (13" M2, macOS 13.6) and completed MDM enrollment but I'm blocked from installing Homebrew and the VSCode extension installer errors with 'operation not permitted'. Also Software Update shows 'Updates are managed by your organization' and the macOS 14 upgrade isn't available. Any guidance?

it-support: Welcome @alex! New-hires are enrolled into a restricted profile during initial onboarding which disables local admin and locks some update settings until we finish the post-enroll jobs. Can you paste the exact error you see when running the Homebrew installer?

alex: Running `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"` returns: "Error: Permission denied @ rb_sysopen - /usr/local/bin/brew" and Installer.app for VSCode fails with "The operation couldn’t be completed. Permission denied (os/kern)".

it-support: That indicates no write access to /usr/local. We normally recommend using the dev container (Docker) for dev tools that need root, but we can grant temporary admin if you need local installs. @emily do you want to grant @alex sudo for 4 hours?

emily: Granted 4 hours.

alex: Thanks. With sudo Homebrew installed to /opt/homebrew fine. But Software Update still shows the text 'Updates are managed by your organization' and macOS Sonoma (14.x) isn't offered. Is that because we pin the OS until dev-images are validated?
\it-support: Exactly. We block major macOS upgrades for 30 days after a new image is released to ensure our MDM & VPN stack compatibility. The banner you're seeing is from our MDM policy that sets the restricted software update payload. You can still apply security updates if we push them, but major upgrades are disabled for Tiers > dev.
\alex: Got it. One more weird thing: FileVault didn't prompt at setup. I enabled it manually, but `fdesetup status` shows "FileVault is On." However the macbot didn't show an escrow message in this thread. How do I confirm the recovery key was captured?
\it-support: run `fdesetup status` (you did) and then check our KMS via the portal, but I can check too if you paste the serial.
\alex: Serial: C02P4Q9L0YH
\it-support: Looking... I don't see a KMS record for that serial. Sometimes the escrow job fails if the machine hasn't checked in post-encrypt. Try `sudo profiles renew -type enrollment` to force check-in, then toggle Wi-Fi (or try ethernet) to ensure connectivity.
\alex: Ran the renew, output: "Enrollment profile: success, lastCheckin: now". Waiting a minute...
\macbot: [automated] FileVault personal recovery key escrow pending for device C02P4Q9L0YH.
\it-support: Looks like the escrow job queued; give it a minute.
\macbot: [automated] FileVault personal recovery key escrowed to KMS for device C02P4Q9L0YH.
\alex: Confirmed, thanks.
\security: Quick note: since you installed Homebrew and may pull packages, please avoid running `sudo brew` for anything that isn't vetted. We have a dev-tools channel for pre-approved packages; @dev-tools will help with any special libs.
\dev-tools: Welcome! If you need things like llvm, postgres, or tmate, we have tap packages and container images—tell us what you need and we can either whitelist a Homebrew formula or provide a container image.
\alex: One last question  when I try to install an older Intel-only binary, macOS asks to install Rosetta. Is that allowed?
\it-support: We allow Rosetta for dev machines if you need to run Intel apps. Use the official prompt to install. If anything asks for a kernel extension or system extension, ping us before approving.
\alex: All set. Thanks for the quick onboarding help everyone!
\emily: Welcome to Redwood, @alex  DM us if anything else pops up.
